Re: Appeal of denial for knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy  
CPT 29881  
Reference number: POC-9F671E8F0E-86300  
Date of adverse benefit determination: August 7, 2026

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy, CPT 29881. The medical record demonstrates a prolonged, documented trial of conservative treatment, persistent functional impairment, and a structural meniscal injury with mechanical locking.

I have experienced 14 months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest. Conservative treatment included all of the following:

- Sixteen weeks of supervised physical therapy from March 4, 2026, through June 24, 2026, with 18 completed visits. Treatment focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion. This course is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- Four months of NSAID treatment, with inadequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 4, 2026, which provided only two weeks of partial relief.

Despite these measures, I continue to experience pain, locking, and giving way. I cannot squat or kneel and am limited to level walking. Examination shows positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

The July 10, 2026, MRI provides objective evidence of a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. The MRI also documents preserved articular cartilage and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes. These findings support the need to address a mechanically displaced meniscal tear after unsuccessful nonoperative treatment.

The record also documents that there is no active infection, untreated substance use, or other stated medical barrier to surgery. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker. The requested procedure was recommended by Okafor, MD, an orthopedic surgeon.

The submitted records therefore document:

1. Prolonged symptoms lasting 14 months;
2. Failure of rest and activity tolerance measures;
3. A completed 16-week supervised physical therapy program with 18 visits;
4. Four months of NSAID treatment without adequate relief;
5. Only brief partial relief from a corticosteroid injection;
6. Persistent locking, giving way, pain-related motion loss, and major functional limitations; and
7. MRI-confirmed displaced bucket-handle medial meniscus tear with mechanical locking.

I request that Wellpoint overturn the denial and approve CPT 29881. If the denial is upheld, please provide the complete medical-necessity criteria actually applied to this request, including the applicable policy or guideline title, policy number or document identifier, version, effective date, and the specific criteria that were not met. I have not been provided the governing policy text, so this appeal does not quote or paraphrase undisclosed policy language.

Please also consider the enclosed supporting documentation:

- Orthopedic surgery clinical note from Okafor, MD;
- MRI report dated July 10, 2026;
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 18 visits from March 4 through June 24, 2026;
- Medication and treatment history;
- Corticosteroid injection record dated May 4, 2026; and
- Relevant examination and functional findings.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and notify me of the determination in writing.

Sincerely,

Skyler Brooks
